newsitem.title: INDIA: Congress for low caste party rule in Indian state.
newsitem.headline: Congress for low caste party rule in Indian state.

text.p: The Congress party appealed on Sunday to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's ruling coalition to support a low caste party leader in India's most populous state of Uttar Pradesh after inconclusive elections there.
Congress's appeal to Deve Gowda's United Front coalition, made by party chief Sitaram Kesri, was aimed at excluding the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) from power in the key state.

Local polls held in Uttar Pradesh last week produced a hung assembly. The right-wing BJP emerged as the largest single party with 177 seats in the 425-seat assembly, but failed to obtain the overall majority it sought.
Congress formed an alliance with the low caste Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), led by Mayawati, and together they captured 100 seats. The United Front was in second place with 134 seats.
"I have been authorised by the party high command to talk to United Front leaders and reiterate our commitment to make Mayawati as the chief minister," Kesri told a news conference.

Congress, which gives Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition crucial backing in the federal parliament in New Delhi, said that in exchange the United Front must support the team under Mayawati in Uttar Pradesh to form a government.

Kesri was speaking after a meeting of the Congress Working Committee, his party's highest decision-making group, which proposed discussions with Deve Gowda and United Front leaders on strategies to keep the BJP from taking power in Uttar Pradesh.
Kesri ruled out any relationship with the BJP, saying: "Congress will never have any adjustment with the BJP in any form".
The BJP's rivals call it "communal" because it alienates minority Moslems.
"Congress has already committed to support the candidature of Mayawati as chief minister and this commitment is irrevocable," he said.
But Deve Gowda's key alliance partner in Uttar Pradesh, the Samajwadi Party, is opposed to Mayawati. The differences are linked to the complex Hindu caste structure.

Samajwadi leader Mulayam Singh Yadav, who is Deve Gowda's defence minister, is backed by peasant caste farmers. Mayawati's Dalit, or former untouchable, supporters often work on their lands. The two formed a coalition in 1993, but later fell out.
The BSP leadership has threatened that if the United Front did not lend support, it would explore possibilities of joining hands with the BJP.
